questions.q: A QR code displayed on a kiosk leads to a spoofed login page. Which threat vector is this?
questions.explain: QR codes and visual content are classified as image-based; quishing is the phishing variant.

questions.q: An attacker uses PowerShell and WMI already present on the system without dropping any files. Which vector is this?
questions.explain: Native endpoint tools represent an endpoint-based vector, detectable through behavioral telemetry.

questions.q: Which vectors belong to the supply chain? (Select all that apply)
options: Software vendor whose update is malicious
USB drive left in the parking lot
questions.explain: MSPs, software vendors, and SaaS providers are trusted third parties: supply chain-based. A USB drive is an external media-based vector.

questions.q: Match each scenario to its threat vector.

pairs.left: NFC badge read by a hostile phone
Exposed RDP with a weak password

questions.explain: The vector family is determined by the entry path, not the final tool used.

questions.q: An APT is primarily distinguished by:
options: A single highly destructive piece of malware
A targeted, persistent, and well-resourced campaign
questions.explain: APT describes the campaign (targeting, duration, resources), not a specific tool.

questions.q: Which vector applies to an industrial controller / SCADA system?
questions.explain: Industrial operational technology systems fall under the OT-based vector, distinct from physical and IoT.
